title: Count one buffer's bytes
prompt: buffer_bytes(devices, size, elem, written, stride) returns the bytes UIR_COPY moves for one buffer of a device loop: size elements of elem bytes each, written if the loop stores to it, and stride its S, or 0 when it is replicated. The replicated case is right. The sharded case has two mistakes. Fix them so that x, w and o of c_shard_scale give 64, 16 and 128.
hints: Look at the sharded case only. What does one device's copy in hold: the whole buffer or its shard?
A sharded copy in is devices * stride * elem, not size. A written buffer is copied in and then back out again, so its count is added to, not replaced.
moved starts at devices * stride * elem, and when written it becomes moved + devices * stride * elem: twice the copy in.
explain: Scatter copies every buffer to every device: the whole buffer when it is replicated, stride elements when it is sharded. Gather copies back only the written shards, the same stride elements per device. So a read-only shard costs devices * stride * elem bytes, a written one twice that, and a replicated buffer devices * size * elem.
